aiSummary.oneLiner: An experimental meta-framework designed to enable spatiotemporal composability in modern distributed web architectures.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Cordis introduces a programming paradigm focused heavily on spatiotemporal composability. It aims to provide developers with a highly structured way to build applications where state, time, and spatial execution contexts are treated as first-class, composable primitives. The framework is currently under active development and serves as the reference implementation for an academic paper on spatiotemporal composability. It allows complex event-driven and stateful logic to be composed seamlessly across different architectural layers of a modern distributed application.
keyFeatures: Spatiotemporal Paradigm: Treats execution contexts and temporal states explicitly as composable building blocks for application logic.
Meta-Framework Architecture: Designed to operate above standard web frameworks to orchestrate complex, distributed logic patterns.
Advanced Effect Management: Provides specialized tools and patterns for managing side effects cleanly in distributed environments.
Academic Foundation: Directly implements and explores the concepts outlined in the paper 'A Programming Paradigm for Spatiotemporal Composability'.
Experimental API: Offers a bleeding-edge API tailored for researchers exploring new paradigms in state and event management.
